title: From commit to running release
summary: Follow one change through CI, an exact-source artifact, infrastructure deployment and a service release. Ask what each green check proves, and for which identity.
opening_answer: CI picks the evidence a change needs and records the tested source. CD accepts only a successful Main push, deploys that source, scans the candidate and the retained rollback image, then promotes service versions behind a smoke and rollback path.

blocks.text: **Build** makes and records an image. **Deploy** updates infrastructure and configuration. **Release** moves a service alias to a candidate image and checks it. Separating them shows where a failure happened and what can be retried.

CI runs on pull requests, Main pushes, manual dispatch and weekly. A path classifier picks checks: owner lanes for fast feedback; shared inputs, workflow changes or unclassified paths select Full verification, the broad source-bound gate.

sections.title: The artifact is useful only with its identity

blocks.text: Tags can be reused and commit labels do not name image bytes. The build verifier records image configuration identifiers and checks runtime user (and Lambda identity); scan receipts bind to configuration and source SHA.

CI uploads per run and attempt: selection artifact, coverage fragments, image receipts, scan evidence. A missing fragment is never an empty success; the receipt’s source SHA is the tested code, not the PR head.
CD validates workflow name, event, head repository, SHA and attempt, then downloads that run’s artifacts. PR runs, fork branches named Main and manual runs are rejected.

CI run identity = repository + event + commit SHA + run ID + attempt
Candidate identity = checked-out source + image config/digest + scan receipt

blocks.title: Two identity checks
blocks.text: Source SHA proves which code was tested; image configuration or digest proves which bytes were checked. A tag proves neither.

sections.title: Deployment and release have different rollback boundaries

spec.title: CD: deploy and promote

steps.label: Accept CI run
steps.detail: Refuses PR, failed, foreign-repository or non-push runs.

steps.label: Deploy stack
steps.detail: Infrastructure and configuration reconciled; on live also the short lane and database split (AD-29).

steps.label: Release owner
steps.detail: Picks changed owner images, scans candidate and retained rollback image (AD-28), checks migration compatibility.

steps.label: Smoke or restore
steps.detail: Pass keeps the candidate; fail restores the previous alias.

spec.caption: Serialized: environment journal and account capacity are shared.

blocks.text: `Deploy` includes owner image promotion and stack adoption; then the upload-to-playback smoke runs. Manual dispatch has preflight, rehearsal and image-verification modes; say which ran. Report stack update and smoke separately. Receipt: CI `39415935595`, CD `39416747925` (attempt 1), source `629119c5b3bd390ce072df0a43fe926cd7a161c7`.

**Admission (AD-28).** Scans cover candidate and retained rollback image. A new advisory hitting only the retained image becomes `RETAINED_FIXABLE`: listed, not blocking, gate not bypassed; the candidate must scan clean. Smoke retries a cold-database login. Run 39644028238 delivered the lane and database split.

**Rollback boundary.** Dropping a field can break the previous image, so releases use additive migrations and an operator attestation that both images fit the schema head. Rollback restores code and aliases, not schema.

sections.title: Use real receipts to explain failure

blocks.text: Full CI `39415935595` passed on `629119c` (25 jobs succeeded; three intentional skips incl. two unconfigured advisory Sonar jobs). CD `39416747925` admitted it; Deploy finished 12:04:26 UTC, smoke 12:06:34 UTC: upload 204, job `done`, encoder exit 0, MP4 and HLS playback passed. AWS read-back matched three image manifests, ten Lambda aliases and the ECS worker definition. Point-in-time, not team acceptance.

blocks.q: Why can a successful CI run still be rejected by CD?
blocks.a: Possibly a pull-request, other-repository or non-push run. CD requires success for a push to Main here, with exact run identity.

blocks.q: If release smoke fails, what does rollback restore?
blocks.a: The previous image alias; schema is not reversed, so migrations must stay compatible with both versions.

blocks.q: Does a green rollback job mean the candidate worked?
blocks.a: No. The candidate may have failed as expected and the known-good alias been restored. Report smoke and restoration separately.

blocks.q: Why not release by tag alone?
blocks.a: Tags can be reused. CD checks source and run identity; receipts bind source to an image configuration or digest.

blocks.q: What is the key explanation when a deploy fails after infrastructure updates?
blocks.a: Name the stage that passed, the later one that failed, the evidence identity, and whether the cause was product, orchestration or a deliberate gate.

takeaways: CI selects by changed paths; uncertainty selects broader verification.
A green tier proves only its selected checks; Full adds inherited acceptance, combined coverage and exact candidate evidence.
Tie every receipt to repository, event, source SHA, attempt and image identity.
Deploy changes infrastructure; release promotes an image behind smoke and restoration, scanning candidate and retained rollback (AD-28).
Image rollback does not roll back schema; use additive migrations.
